html:
The Great Mosque of Samarra was built from 848 to 851 by the Abbasid caliph al-Mutawakkil in Samarra, on the Tigris north of Baghdad. For centuries it was the largest mosque in the world.

Samarra was the capital of the caliphs from 836 to 892, built to house their Turkish soldiers away from Baghdad. The mosque's brick walls enclose a vast space. Its minaret, the Malwiya, is a spiral cone about 52 metres high, with a ramp winding round the outside.

The rest of the mosque is in ruins, and the top of the minaret was damaged by a bomb in 2005, during the Iraq War. The city of Samarra is a World Heritage Site. Compare the ziggurats of ancient Iraq.
